description: Mandatory deterministic fixture (CLAUDE.md, docs/07 §3). Canonical state hashes for the fixed seed + DEFAULT_CONFIG + the fixed command log below (one command of every intervention kind, Milestone 9). Intentional engine behavior changes require an ENGINE_VERSION bump, regenerated hashes (pnpm headless --seed 0xE0A12026 --ticks 10000 --checkpoints 0,1,10,100,1000,10000 --fixture-commands) and a CHANGELOG entry. Engine 0.7.0 regenerated every hash: the canonical stream gained the founder region and the command log, event payloads became signed 32-bit words, the config gained the interventions section, and the fixture now RUNS the command log — the trajectory legitimately diverges from 0.6.0 once the first command applies at tick 50 (by tick 10000: population 4381 vs 4364, 26 drowning deaths from the flooded LOWER_TERRAIN stroke, a meteor crater at the founder centre). Tick 0 and 1 differ from 0.6.0 only through the hash-stream and config changes; the organism trajectory is identical until the first command applies. Engine 0.8.0 regenerated every hash again, for two intentional authoritative changes (ADR 0025): the expected-gain food-target rule replaced the categorical carcass gate (docs/04 §20 as amended), and the plant capacities were calibrated to 0.6x the v0.1 hypothesis (docs/08 §5 as amended, closing L11). The tick-0 hash moves through the config digest alone; the trajectory diverges once feeding decisions begin. The 0.8.0 calibration also moves carcass decay 20 -> 48 (docs/08 §15 as amended). By tick 10000 the leaner, scavenging world holds population 1003 (was 4381), 1382 live carcasses under the 4096 cap (was pinned at it), and has eaten 511.4k meat units (was 0 on the pre-policy reference world). Engine 0.9.0 (M14, docs/11 §M14) regenerated every hash for one intentional authoritative change: organisms carry a 27-gene morphological genome, inherited and mutated like the ecological one and hashed with it, so the canonical stream is longer and the PRNG stream gains 27 classification draws per birth. Tick 0 moves through the config digest and the founder bodies; the trajectory diverges from the first birth, because morphological mutation consumes draws that ecological and brain mutation used to consume. Morphology has no physical consequence yet — that is M15 — so the ecological trajectory is the same rules on a different random stream. Engine 0.10.0 (M15, docs/11 §M15, ADR 0029) regenerated every hash for one intentional authoritative change: the developed body now has physical consequence. A centralized PhysicalPhenotype turns morphology into sixteen multipliers on mass, energy storage, basal upkeep, growth cost, top speed, acceleration, turn rate, water performance, armor, attack, bite size, vision range and arc, thermal tolerance, contact extent and offspring construction cost. The founder body is exactly neutral in all sixteen, so tick 0 moves only through the config digest — the new organism.physicalMorphology block — and the founder population's physics is bit-for-bit the ecology Milestones 0–13 calibrated. The trajectory diverges from the first birth, when a mutated body first weighs, moves, eats and costs something different from its parent's. By tick 10000 the fixture world holds population 1841 with 555.3k meat units eaten, 5301 births and 3460 deaths. Only the tick-10000 checkpoint moved from the first 0.10.0 regeneration: flooring offspringCostFactorQ at Q (a birth must never create energy) changes nothing until a parent lighter than the founder reproduces, which on this seed happens after tick 1000. Engine 0.11.0 (M16, docs/11 §M16, ADR 0030) regenerated every hash for one intentional authoritative change on four counts: the neural topology genome is inherited state and joins the canonical stream; authoritative neural state (memory registers and carried hidden activations) joins it as its own section; the weight block grew 400 -> 576 for the recurrent and memory blocks; and structural mutation adds draws at every birth. Tick 0 moves through the config digest, the wider genome and the founder's topology; the trajectory diverges from the first birth. The founder's brain costs exactly zero upkeep by construction, so M16 does not re-tune the calibrated ecology by existing — but brain upkeep is a real drain on any lineage that grows one, and by tick 10000 the fixture world holds population 1262 with 460.2k meat units eaten, 4401 births and 3139 deaths. Every checkpoint moved twice inside 0.11.0 before it shipped, both times for a defect this fixture and its neighbours caught. First, the inheritance copy in resolveReproduction still copied 400 weights into a 576-wide scratch buffer reused by every birth, so each child inherited the previous child's recurrent and memory weights (ADR 0030 §8); that moved the tick-10000 checkpoint alone, because nothing diverges until the second birth. Then the complexity coefficients were recalibrated: charging a whole energy per connection made one usable hidden unit cost an adult's entire basal bill, and measurement found hidden units being switched on by mutation and removed by selection every time (ADR 0030 §9a). The coefficients are Q-scaled now, so the config digest changes and every checkpoint including tick 0 moves with it. Engine 0.12.0 (M17, docs/11 §M17, ADR 0031) regenerated every hash for one intentional authoritative change on five counts: the environment carries five biomass and five capacity planes instead of one; the ecological genome went from 16 loci to 22 (the signed `diet` locus out, six per-channel `Process` loci and `ToxinResistance` in); the brain's input layer widened 20 -> 32 for the per-channel densities and gradients, taking the weight block to 780; feeding ranks six channels where it ranked two; and digestive and toxin-resistance upkeep join the basal cost. Tick 0 moves through the config digest and the wider genome, and the trajectory diverges immediately because the founders are standing on ground that now holds five resources. By tick 10000 the fixture world holds population 1468 with 6201 births and 4733 deaths — and 3164 of those deaths are TOXIN, against 1538 starvation. Defended growth is the leading cause of death in the shipped world: a lineage whose processing drifts away from foliage finds the richest channel is the poisonous one, and pays for it until it evolves resistance or better foliage processing. The population is stable through it (M16: 1262), so this is a hazard the ecology absorbs rather than one that collapses it. Engine 0.12.1 regenerated every hash for one intentional authoritative change (ADR 0031 §5e): plant regrowth no longer has a flat production floor. The seed bank added `seedBankRegenUnits` to any cell below a per-channel `minRegenThreshold`, a term independent of capacity, growth rate and grazing pressure, so a grazed cell was topped up forever; accounted one environment step at tick 40000 of the soak world, it was supplying 87.4% of all plant production against 12.6% from the logistic term capacity governs. That is why M17's 100000-tick soak sat at exactly `limits.maxOrganisms` and why cutting that capacity by a further 70% still reached it — a 70% cut bought at most a factor of 2.3 in population, against an uncensored 18712 for the unscaled world. The seed bank now fires only on a cell emptied to exactly zero, which is what its own comment always said it did, and `minRegenThreshold` is removed from ResourceProfile rather than set small, because a threshold is the shape of mistake that reopens this. Tick 0 moves through the config digest alone — the removed field — and the trajectory diverges as soon as grazing first empties a cell. By tick 10000 the fixture world holds population 650 (was 1468) with 2452 births and 1802 deaths, and the death profile is the change worth reading: 886 toxin against 896 starvation, where 0.12.0 recorded 3164 toxin against 1538. Defended growth is no longer the leading cause of death. A flat per-cell subsidy is worth most to whatever has the highest energyPerUnit, because it arrives in units and is converted at the channel's own rate, so the seed bank had been quietly paying organisms to eat the poisonous channel.
